newsitem.title: UK: Options, interest rates mesmerise gold market.
newsitem.headline: Options, interest rates mesmerise gold market.

text.p: Precious metals prices clung to tiny ranges on Tuesday morning as the gold market held its breath ahead of an over-the-counter options expiry.
The prospect of a widely expected rise in U.S. interest rates at a Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting later in the day was also keeping the market on edge.
Gold fixed little changed at $350.90 an ounce, compared to $350.20 on Monday afternoon. Prices were not seen straying far from the psychological $350 level ahead of the expiry.
"The options expiry is the only potentially market moving feature," one dealer said, referring to the 1430 GMT expiry.
"I expect there will be a fight around $350 which is the main strike price," he said, adding that following the expiry of March options, prices were expected to ease modestly.
An expected U.S. interest rate hike of 25 basis points by the FOMC was already priced into the market, but the market would watch closely for any surprises, dealers said.

"The FOMC will only affect the market it they don't raise rates at all or raise them by half a percentage point," a dealer said, adding that a bigger than expected rise may depress precious metals prices while boosting the dollar.
Silver was similarly static, trading in a two-cent range.
It was last indicated slightly firmer at $5.17/$5.19, up four cents, and the market was expected to focus on the $5.15 strike price ahead of the expiry, dealers said.
"After the expiry if prices come off the $5.10 level should hold, but if it doesn't we will see silver much lower," a dealer said.
Silver had tested its key support level at $5.10 on Monday, then rebounded higher after that floor held.
Platinum was slightly firmer and holding steady, with no repeat so far of Monday's depressive bout of selling out of Switzerland, dealers said.
Some dealers cast doubt on market rumours that the metal had been shipped from Russia, a key producer of platinum and especially palladium.
"I tend to think it wasn't Russian -- why make a sudden shipment and if so why not also sell palladium?" a dealer said.
The market was still waiting for news on delayed Russian supply talks on palladium with key importer Japan, he added.
Platinum was last indicated at $376.00/$377.00, up $1.00, and palladium was little changed at $148.00/$149.00, up $0.50.
